method: For every cohort lemma the full OEWN 2025 candidate set (all parts of speech) was read from the verified archive. Each candidate is either SELECTED (a learner sense for a Bangladeshi English learner) or REJECTED with a reason. Definitions are the exact OEWN definitions; OEWN examples are listed as evidence only and are never reused. Bangla meanings, explanations and English/Bangla examples are Ovidhan editorial text (origin OVIDHAN_EDITORIAL).

words.more_than_three_justification: Challenge pass: all four selected senses are materially distinct and each is a high-frequency learner use. They differ in what is judged (quality of a thing, skill of a person, moral character, benefit to someone), in the Bangla word a learner needs (ভালো, দক্ষ/পটু, সৎ ও নীতিবান, উপকারী) and in the English frame (good + noun, good at, a good person, good for). Merging any two would hide a pattern. The other 23 candidates were re-read against these four and are redundant, idiomatic, narrow or nonstandard (see the per-candidate reasons).
words.order_rationale: The V1 general sense stays first: it is the broadest and most frequent meaning. The skill, moral and beneficial senses follow in order of learner frequency.

rejected.reason: Trade/commerce noun (a commodity); technical and not what learners mean by 'good'.
Abstract noun counterpart of the selected moral-character sense (goodness); low independent learner value.
Abstract philosophical noun ('the good'); low learner value.
Idiomatic noun use ('for your own good', 'what is the good of'); overlaps the selected beneficial sense and is better taught as a phrase.
Quantifier use ('a good mile'); idiomatic and rare for learners.
Close-relationship reading ('a good friend'): learners understand it from the general sense (ভালো বন্ধু); the 'close/intimate' nuance is better taught with 'close friend'.
Narrow intensifier use ('a good cleaning'); low priority.
Vague 'generally admired' gloss ('good taste'); overlaps the general V1 sense.
Validity sense ('a warranty good for two years'); administrative and rare for general learners.
Pattern 'it is a good thing that'; covered by the general V1 sense.
Food-freshness use ('the milk is still good'): real but a narrow collocation of the general 'acceptable condition' meaning, and not a distinct pattern learners need to be taught.
Not forged (counterfeit money); specialist and rare.
Duplicates the selected moral sense (02052395-a); the selected synset is the richer one.
Near-duplicate of the selected beneficial sense; 'good for health' is shown in that sense's usage.
Excellent physical condition ('good teeth'); covered by the general V1 sense.
Vague 'appealing to the mind' gloss ('good music'); covered by the general V1 sense.

Agreeable or pleasing ('a good time', 'good weather'): frequent, but it is the general 'desirable' meaning applied to experiences; the OEWN gloss is vague and it needs no different English frame or Bangla word (ভালো).
Suitability use ('a good time to plant'); covered by the general V1 sense.
Capable of pleasing ('good looks'); narrow, collocation-driven.
Formal 'deserving of esteem' cluster ('a good name'); low learner frequency.
Financially safe ('a good investment'); finance-specific.
OEWN itself marks this adverb as a nonstandard dialectal variant of 'well'; not taught as standard.
Informal intensifier ('beat him good'); informal and nonstandard.

words.risk_note: 27 OEWN candidates; four senses are kept and 23 are rejected. The exclusion choices are judgement calls a reviewer may want to revisit. Challenge pass: the V1 Bangla example translation was unnatural ('প্রতিরাত পড়ে সে ভালো ফল করেছিল'); V2 now teaches an improved translation and keeps the exact V1 text only as the parity/traceability record (v1_revision), so V1 wording is not preferred merely for parity.

selected.reason: V1 primary sense: the general 'desirable or positive qualities' meaning. OEWN definition and synset retained verbatim; the Bangla example translation is improved (v1_revision).
The 'good at' skill sense: high frequency and a different Bangla word from the general sense.
A good person: moral character, clearly separate from quality or skill.
The 'good for' beneficial sense (good for your health): the general OEWN synset for benefit, preferred over the narrower health-only synset.

v1_learner_gap.description: V1 teaches only the general 'having desirable qualities' adjective. It misses the three high-frequency frames good at (skill), a good person (moral character) and good for (beneficial), each of which needs a different Bangla word.

v1_sense_revision.reason: The V1 Bangla example translation ('প্রতিরাত পড়ে সে ভালো ফল করেছিল') is unnatural Bangla ('প্রতিরাত' is not used with 'পড়ে' like this). V2 teaches the natural translation; the exact V1 text is kept only so V1 parity and traceability remain provable.

words.order_rationale: The V1 title/name sense stays first: it is the use Bangladeshi learners meet most (forms, job letters). The appointment sense follows because it also concerns offices and posts, then the general act of officially designating a place or thing.
words.risk_note: Challenge pass: both OEWN action senses were added after re-reading all three candidates. The first rejection reason ('derivational, better taught with the verb') was withdrawn because the act senses are a different, genuinely used pattern (designation of X as Y). OEWN has no separate 'position/post' synset: the title sense (V1) is the one that covers an official title or name, and the position idea is carried by the appointment sense.

selected.reason: V1 primary sense: the title/name meaning (an official title or name by which someone or something is called and classified) that Bangladeshi learners meet on forms and job documents. Retained verbatim.

The act of putting a person into a non-elective post (designation as director). Materially distinct from the title noun: it names an action done to a person, with a different Bangla word (নিয়োগ, মনোনয়ন).

The act of designating or identifying something (designation of a place as protected). Distinct from both the title noun and the person-appointment sense: its object is a thing or place, with its own Bangla rendering (ঘোষণা, চিহ্নিতকরণ).

v1_learner_gap.description: V1 teaches only the title/name noun (পদবি), which is the dominant sense on forms and job documents. It misses the two action uses that appear in formal and news English: appointing someone to a post ('her designation as director') and officially naming or declaring something ('the designation of the fort as a protected site').

words.more_than_three_justification: Challenge pass: 'tough' has four common, materially distinct learner senses with four different Bangla renderings and four different things being described: a hard task or situation (কঠিন), a person's temperament (কঠোর ও শক্ত মনের), a well-made object (মজবুত, টেকসই) and food that is hard to chew (শক্ত, চিবানো কঠিন). The sturdy/durable sense is supported by OEWN synset 00714724-a ('substantially made or constructed'; sturdy, tough) and is not covered by any other selected sense.
words.order_rationale: The V1 'difficult' sense stays first: it is the most frequent use (a tough exam, a tough decision). The personality sense follows, then the strong/durable object sense, then the food sense.

rejected.reason: Informal noun for a cruel, brutal person; overlaps the personality sense and is rare as a noun.
Slang noun for a violent young criminal; informal and potentially stigmatising.
Boxing-specific noun (a street fighter).
OEWN marks this as an occasional colloquial use for 'bad' (feeling unwell); not a standard learner sense.
Hard to comprehend or solve ('a tough question'): the V1 'difficult' sense and its exam example already teach this use, and both render as কঠিন; not materially distinct.
Unfortunate or hard to bear ('tough luck', 'a tough break'): the hardship meaning is already in the V1 sense ('a tough life'); the fixed expressions are better taught as phrases.
Physically toughened (tough soles of the feet); narrow and rare.
Violent and lawless (tough street gangs); overlaps the personality sense and risks stereotyping.

words.risk_note: Challenge pass: the strong/sturdy/durable physical sense was reconsidered and added; the earlier 'stay within three' reason was removed because the three-sense target is not a limit. Eight of twelve candidates remain rejected, each on its own merits.

selected.reason: V1 primary sense: difficult or demanding. Retained verbatim.
A tough person: not gentle or sentimental. Different from 'difficult' and common in everyday English.
Strong, durable, well-made things (tough boots, tough fabric). Materially distinct from difficulty, temperament and food texture; OEWN lists tough with 'sturdy' in this synset.
Tough meat: resistant to cutting or chewing. A classic learner sense that no other selected sense covers.

v1_learner_gap.description: V1 teaches only 'difficult / demanding'. It misses the personality sense (a tough, unsentimental person), the strong/durable physical sense (tough boots, tough fabric) and the food sense (tough meat), all common and with different Bangla words.
